title: The Front Porch
novel:
Ted [[discovered|discover]] a shocking truth. Lily had been [[sabotaging|sabotage]] his relationships for years. She would find faults in his girlfriends and quietly [[manipulate|manipulate]] Ted into breaking up with them.

"You did what?!" Ted [[exploded|explode]].

Lily was [[defensive|defensive]]. "I was protecting you," she [[claimed|claim]]. "They weren't good enough for you."

The [[revelation|revelation]] [[shattered|shatter]] Ted's trust. He felt [[betrayed|betray]] by one of his closest friends. "How could you make my decisions for me?" he asked.

Marshall was caught in the middle. He knew about Lily's [[interference|interference]] but had stayed silent. "I didn't want to [[upset|upset]] either of you," he [[admitted|admit]].

Lily [[explained|explain]] her [[philosophy|philosophy]]. "I picture us old, sitting on the front porch together. If I can't picture your girlfriend on that porch, she doesn't belong."

Ted was [[stunned|stun]]. "That's not your choice to make."

The gang argued for hours. Robin said Lily was [[controlling|control]]. Barney said she was [[brilliant|brilliant]]. Marshall said nothing.

Finally, Lily [[apologized|apologize]]. "I'm sorry. I should have let you make your own mistakes."

Ted [[forgave|forgive]] her — slowly. But the front porch test would never feel the same again.

revelation.en: a surprising truth that is revealed

interference.en: getting involved in someone else's business

upset.en: to make someone feel sad or worried

admit.en: to agree that something is true

philosophy.en: a way of thinking about things

forgive.en: to stop being angry at someone
